questions: Does wheel_track 0.08 m lower max_error below 0.06 m on the s-bend and slalom, or has the turn-rate gain stopped helping?
Does steering_oscillation rise sharply at the narrower track, which would show the controller is over-turning?
Where does the first off-track event occur, and is it preceded by a line-loss event or by a steady drift?
Does progress now respond to base_speed, or is it still fixed by off-track ends?

intent: Continue the wheel_track trend that lifted the score in iteration 3. Narrowing the track from 0.09 m to 0.08 m raises turn rate per unit of wheel differential, aiming to pull max_error below the 0.06 m off-track floor on the s-bend and slalom. Sensors, body, mass and wheel radius stay as in iteration 3 so the result isolates the track change. Expected: progress above 0.18 on the s-bend and slalom, with line loss at or below iteration 3 levels.
learning: Iteration 3 showed that narrowing wheel_track from 0.12 m to 0.09 m gave a net gain of about 2.8 points, driven by the s-bend. Sensor lead at y=0.07 and the shorter, lighter body both cut the score, so they stay reverted. Off-track is set by max_error reaching the 0.06 m floor, so the next levers are turn rate (wheel_track) and ground speed (wheel_radius). Track narrowing is tested now; wheel_radius is the next candidate if progress stalls.
rationale: Iteration 3 (wheel_track 0.09 m) is the best design so far at 57.9, up from 55.1 for the iteration 1 baseline. The gain came from the s-bend (progress 0.163 to 0.178, control effort up, max_error still at the 0.063 m floor), while the oval slipped slightly and slalom was flat. Every run still ends off_track, and max_error sits at the 0.06 m floor on all tracks, so the limit is still turn authority and tracking lag, not sensor coverage. Line loss is now rare (oval 0, s-bend 0.1, slalom 1.0). Sensor lead at y=0.07 and the lighter short body both hurt in iteration 2, so I keep y=0.05, the 7-sensor, 16 mm, +/-0.06 m array, and the 0.18 m body at 0.8 kg. The off-track floor is fixed at 0.06 m for any allowed body width, so body width stays at 0.12 m. The one geometry lever that moved the result was wheel_track, since turn rate is (vR - vL)/wheel_track. I therefore continue that trend by one step, from 0.09 m to 0.08 m (the allowed minimum), and change nothing else, so the race isolates the turn-rate effect. Expected result: the s-bend and slalom progress rise further and max_error falls slightly, with a modest risk of more steering_oscillation. If oscillation climbs and progress does not improve, I will return to 0.09 m and test wheel_radius for ground speed instead.
